RBAC lives on the API server; etcd doesn't enforce it. So don't go through `kubectl get secret` — go through the datastore. In this kind cluster the control-plane node is the container `dojo-control-plane`: `docker exec dojo-control-plane ...` puts you on the node, where etcd's client certs sit at `/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/`.

etcd keys objects under `/registry`. Secrets are at `/registry/secrets/<namespace>/<name>` — here, `/registry/secrets/dojo-etcd/vault-backup`. Use `ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl` with `--cacert=ca.crt --cert=server.crt --key=server.key` from that pki dir to `get` that key. The `ETCDCTL_API=3` prefix is mandatory or the query hits the wrong API version.

The stored value is a binary protobuf blob with the plaintext inside (no encryption at rest), so pipe the `get` through `strings | grep KUBE`. Full one-liner: `docker exec dojo-control-plane sh -c 'ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key get /registry/secrets/dojo-etcd/vault-backup' | strings | grep KUBE`. If `etcdctl` isn't on the node PATH, run the same command via `kubectl -n kube-system exec etcd-dojo-control-plane -- ...`.
